rv.q: As is, lacking more adept staging, I found this adaptation hewed too closely to the source material to excite throughout.
More than 180 years after Dupin first appeared, Theatre 40 makes a convincing case that Poe’s original detective still deserves the spotlight.

This program will get anyone into the spirit (pun?) of the season with the solving of mysteries that occurred back when gay Paree was a bit glum and darker that the city of lights could have mustered up.

cn.t: Michael Mullen delivers an impossible-to-ignore performance as Poe's pioneering detective in this well-received adaptation, bringing Edgar Allan Poe's trio of mystery tales to vivid life on stage.
